pack.description: Vocabulary of art history passages and talks: techniques, styles, patrons and interpretation.
pack.selection_note: Internal selection of terms that recur in introductory art history texts; this is not an official list and CEFR levels are author estimates.
pack.copyright_policy: Original content written for this app. No dictionary definition, ETS item or external word list was copied.

entries.definition: a picture painted directly on a wall or ceiling while the plaster is still wet
entries.example_academic: The fresco had to be completed section by section before the plaster dried.
entries.example_spoken: There's a huge fresco on the ceiling of the chapel.

entries.definition: the way in which the parts of a picture, piece of music or text are arranged
entries.example_academic: The diagonal composition draws the viewer's eye toward the central figure.
entries.example_spoken: I like the colors, but the composition feels crowded.

entries.definition: the method of drawing that makes some objects look farther away than others; also, a particular way of thinking about something
entries.example_academic: The use of perspective gave Renaissance paintings an unprecedented sense of depth.
entries.example_spoken: From a student's perspective, the new schedule is worse.

entries.definition: a person who gives money or support to an artist, writer or organization
entries.example_academic: Wealthy patrons often dictated the subject and even the colors of a painting.
entries.example_spoken: The gallery depends on a few generous patrons.

entries.definition: to formally ask and pay someone to create a piece of work
entries.example_academic: The city commissioned a monument to mark the end of the war.
entries.example_spoken: The department commissioned a mural for the new building.

entries.definition: to show or describe something in a picture or in words
entries.example_academic: The panel depicts a harvest scene in remarkable detail.
entries.example_spoken: The movie depicts college life pretty accurately.

entries.definition: relating to beauty and the way something looks
entries.example_academic: The choice of material was aesthetic rather than practical.
entries.example_spoken: It's a purely aesthetic change; the app works the same way.

entries.definition: a piece of strong cloth on which an artist paints, or a painting made on it
entries.example_academic: X-rays revealed an earlier portrait beneath the surface of the canvas.
entries.example_spoken: She paints on huge canvases, bigger than the door.

entries.definition: a natural substance that gives color to paint, skin or plants
entries.example_academic: The blue pigment was more expensive than gold and reserved for important figures.
entries.example_spoken: This paint has so much pigment that one coat is enough.

entries.definition: a large picture painted on a wall
entries.example_academic: The murals presented national history to a largely illiterate public.
entries.example_spoken: Students painted a mural on the side of the gym.

entries.definition: the material or method that an artist uses to make a work
entries.example_academic: Oil paint became the dominant medium because it dried slowly and could be reworked.
entries.example_spoken: Clay is my favorite medium to work with.

entries.definition: a shape, image or idea that is repeated in a work of art or literature
entries.example_academic: The lotus motif recurs on pottery, textiles and temple walls.
entries.example_spoken: There's a bird motif all through the wallpaper.

entries.definition: the work of repairing something old so that it looks as it did originally
entries.example_academic: The restoration removed centuries of dirt and revealed unexpectedly bright colors.
entries.example_spoken: The library is closed for restoration until May.

entries.definition: a work of art of outstanding quality, often the best work of its maker
entries.example_academic: The altarpiece is widely regarded as the masterpiece of the northern school.
entries.example_spoken: Your presentation was good, but let's not call it a masterpiece.

entries.definition: a picture made by cutting a design into metal or wood and printing from it
entries.example_academic: Engravings allowed a single composition to circulate in hundreds of copies.
entries.example_spoken: There's an old engraving of the campus in the hallway.

entries.definition: a painting or photograph of objects that do not move, such as fruit, flowers or dishes
entries.example_academic: The still life invited viewers to reflect on the brevity of human pleasures.
entries.example_spoken: We had to draw a still life of three apples and a jug.

entries.definition: the use of strong contrasts between light and dark in a picture
entries.example_academic: Chiaroscuro lends the scene a dramatic intensity that flat lighting could not achieve.
entries.example_spoken: The photographer uses chiaroscuro, like an old painting.

entries.definition: the images and symbols used in a work of art or by a culture, and the study of what they mean
entries.example_academic: The iconography of the tomb combines local gods with imported symbols.
entries.example_spoken: You need to know the iconography to understand who each saint is.

entries.definition: the support, especially money, that a person or institution gives to artists or to a cause
entries.example_academic: Court patronage allowed the workshop to experiment with costly materials.
entries.example_spoken: Without the patronage of that family, he'd never have finished the series.

entries.definition: relating to the highly decorated and dramatic style of European art and music of the 1600s and early 1700s
entries.example_academic: Baroque ceilings dissolve architecture into painted skies crowded with figures.
entries.example_spoken: The church is baroque, so expect a lot of gold.

entries.definition: the artists and thinkers whose new ideas and methods are very different from what is accepted
entries.example_academic: The avant-garde rejected the idea that painting should imitate visible reality.
entries.example_spoken: Her films are a bit too avant-garde for me.

entries.definition: the history of who has owned a work of art or other valuable object
entries.example_academic: Gaps in the provenance raised doubts about whether the painting had been stolen.
entries.example_spoken: The auction house checked the provenance before the sale.

entries.definition: the technique of drawing an object shorter than it really is so that it seems to point toward or away from the viewer
entries.example_academic: Bold foreshortening makes the outstretched arm appear to break through the picture surface.
entries.example_spoken: My drawing looks wrong because I can't do foreshortening.

entries.definition: paint applied so thickly that it stands up from the surface
entries.example_academic: The impasto catches the light and gives the waves a physical presence.
entries.example_spoken: You can see the impasto if you look at the painting from the side.

entries.definition: a picture or story in which the characters and events stand for ideas or moral qualities
entries.example_academic: The fresco is an allegory of good government, with each figure embodying a virtue.
entries.example_spoken: The whole novel is an allegory about power.

entries.definition: a work of art made of three panels placed side by side
entries.example_academic: The outer panels of the triptych could be closed to protect the central scene.
entries.example_spoken: The exhibition opens with a huge triptych.

entries.definition: a thin layer, often green or brown, that forms on metal or other surfaces with age
entries.example_academic: Collectors prize the green patina that bronze acquires over centuries.
entries.example_spoken: The old desk has a nice patina; don't sand it.

entries.definition: the point in a picture where parallel lines seem to meet in the distance
entries.example_academic: All the lines of the tiled floor converge on a single vanishing point.
entries.example_spoken: Put the vanishing point on the horizon and draw the road toward it.

entries.definition: showing people, animals and objects as they really look; also, using words in a non-literal way
entries.example_academic: He returned to figurative painting after a decade of pure abstraction.
entries.example_spoken: I meant it in a figurative sense, not literally.
